Receiving Onesimus as a brother tests love within an unequal relationship

Verse 8 says Paul could command Philemon and chooses to appeal. Verse 16 asks that Onesimus be received as a beloved brother. Verse 17 puts the request in terms of partnership. If Philemon counts Paul a partner, he must receive Onesimus as he would Paul. That puts the returning servant in the apostle’s place at the door. Verse 18 removes the money objection: Paul will pay what is owed. Verse 21 adds that Paul expects Philemon to do even more than he asks.
